records.root_cause_summary: Independent helper-bytes review (separate agent session, finding 381) observation F-01 on run_authority.c (src/xverse/maestro/native/run_authority.c:161 (freeze_all), 391, 517, 498): Authority refreeze is skipped when the close deadline has already elapsed. Scenario: freeze_all() writes cgroup.freeze only while now_ns()<end; close_authority(g,until) at 517 and close_authority(g,g->deadline) at 391 use the just-processed request's own deadline as end. In the release-timeout case this is guaranteed to trigger: RELEASE consumes the ticket, writes '0' (435), then waits while enabled()&&now<ticket_end (436); the loop can only exit by exec completing or by now>=deadline, so on timeout close_authority(g,until) is called with end already passed, every freeze write is skipped, freeze_failed=1 and the reply is REJECTED(reason=PROTOCOL) without the freeze mask. Once closed, the lease-expiry path at 498 never retries. The thawed workload keeps running until Python reacts to REJECTED (affa_client.py:288/408-447 revoke -> SIGKILL -> supervisor cleanup) or the generation ends. The same skip can occur on a CANCEL that arrives with little remaining time, which is then acknowledged CANCELLED(reason=6) with a partial mask. Verified against the source by the implementing session; no runtime reproduction; author disposition pending (helper change with new frozen hashes and a fresh review, or a documented Python-side precondition).

Independent helper-bytes review (separate agent session, finding 381) observation F-02 on run_authority.c (src/xverse/maestro/native/run_authority.c:365-385 (advance_unit)): ADVANCE admits a fresh-generation boundary with no proof it is in the supervisor watch inventory. Scenario: advance_unit checks identity, frozen/empty/leaf, same parent and uniqueness, but the native authority cannot know whether bootstrap.c watches the new leaf; only affa_client.py:273-274 (_watched, 229-240) enforces that before sending. If that Python precondition is bypassed or regresses, a released workload of the advanced generation lies outside the supervisor's freeze set: on authority death the supervisor kills the authority (its only thaw writer) and freezes only watched leaves (bootstrap.c:270-276), so that workload stays running unfenced until Python C1 cleanup or generation end. Verified against the source by the implementing session; no runtime reproduction; author disposition pending (helper change with new frozen hashes and a fresh review, or a documented Python-side precondition).

records.root_cause_summary: F-08/F-09: a schedule/tick statement or teardown record is sent with less remaining time than its normal service time (window end; shared teardown phase deadline), the persistence RPC times out, the channel is failed by design and the terminal records are lost. Limiting term measured under load (428); quiet-host service times per request type (438). First candidate 8184a2b15 (full-budget threshold) rejected by review and A/B (433, 434). v2 f4262c285 refuses a send whose remaining time is below the longest round trip already observed for its kind; A/B b and attribution A/B c on a quiet host: arm B no persist timeout, T3 clean 20/20, every refusal at the T3 active end, no failed node (454, 455). Same-session support only; false-refusal rate under load not measured (453 item 2). Under natural load (467, 469): at load 13-15 the 12 load-sensitive tests fail in most runs with or without v2 (A/B d2: A 20, B 19 failures); v2 replaces persist timeouts by refusals without more failures. The dominant cause is the fixed RPC and phase budgets against host load; v2 narrows F-08/F-09 and does not remove them. Author decision 468 A2: accepted as a partial mitigation only. E1 (897d9dc50, author delegation 476): load-aware interior budgets inside hard admitted bounds; a shared per-run estimator, widening-only interior deadlines and refusal before mutation when the remaining work no longer fits. Natural-load A/B e: A 9 vs B 2 failures, no ML-PERSIST-TIMEOUT or TEARDOWN-INCOMPLETE as dispatcher diagnostics in B; A/B f: A 25 vs B 1, no B-only failure. Reviews FAIL, FAIL, PASS (480, 482, 484). Remaining: active-window exhaustion (outer) and the unwidened restart path. Full runs on E1 (487-491): platform-regression-20261022a-1 gate accepted.

F-10: a lost observation (schedule failure with observation_missing) is recorded as health-loss/unknown over an M3 'unknown' observation, which the design allows; the assessor rejected it three ways (status set, parent-proof requirement, missing handleRef), so a factually complete failed native run was never normal-complete. Causes traced by instrumentation, one at a time (439-443); candidate e9b346a05 accepts the pair, requires dependencies [] and takes handleRef from the issuance of the current generation on both sides (445, 448). Two independent reviews, the second PASS; 35-module regression 362 passed in its own venv.

Verification boundary: the native-started persistence worker runs python -I and imports the interpreter's installed xverse, so a PYTHONPATH=src run mixes versions whenever src differs from the install. No earlier result was affected (installed == main == src at c3a9213a1; 8184a2b15 changed parent-side files only). Candidate tooling: one installed version per arm or run (candidate-venv mkvenv.sh/runv.sh); its first full use omitted the build tools (458) and was repaired.

D-09 design divergence: the terminal path aborts the Argus writer after a failed execution (report never eligible), and the offline verifier sets overall incomplete whenever the writer is not closed, so no failed execution reaches overall complete; the design branch normal-documented-failure expects overall complete with execution failed. Not a defect decision: awaits the author's ruling at T01 (finalize factually complete failed runs, or amend the branch). Author ruling 468 C1: the design branch is kept and the product changed. Candidate cc3d444c1 (471, 472): a report whose only blocker is terminal-outcome and which is otherwise complete and published is finalizable; worker, parent ACK, RunClosure and dispatcher use one predicate; eligibility unchanged. Independent review PASS; three negative controls; D-09 test strict and discriminating.

F-11 (pre-existing): a stale _probe_failure left by a swallowed check_health can be reported for a later failure; every _query failure cancels the owner, so only the diagnostic code can be misattributed (448).

F-12 (pre-existing): between the worker's prepare_generation and the parent's _claims update, or after a failed advance, the two generation counters differ, so a failure statement naming that unit fails ML-SCHEDULE-ACK on the generation field (true at dd00c1db5).
